caption: The drawing depicts an architectural entranceway composed of a large arch constructed with alternating red and white blocks. This arch is supported on both sides by rectangular columns featuring a red tile pattern up to the capitals, which are highlighted in white. The entrance is framed by a red-and-white bordered archway above double wooden doors with visible vertical grain patterns. The ground consists of a patterned tile floor in shades of red and brown, extending from the entrance to the foreground. Above the doorway, there are two red vases, each containing stylized flowers, painted against a pale wall that blends shades of blue, green, and yellow. In the center near the top, there is a recessed niche with a red shell motif above it, and it is flanked by two smaller blue vases with flowers. Behind the arch, wooden ceiling beams are visible, adding further detail to the composition. The artist's signature, "A. Regla," appears in the bottom right corner of the image.
title: Restoration Drawing
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
